title: Tiered usage pricing and invoices
instructions:
Implement graduated usage pricing using integer cents throughout.

## Files
- `pricing.py`

`RateTable(tiers)` copies an iterable of `(upper_bound, unit_cents)` pairs. Bounds
are cumulative quantity limits, not tier widths. There must be at least one tier;
exactly the last bound must be None (unlimited). Finite bounds must be positive
and strictly increasing. Prices must be nonnegative. Invalid tables raise
`ValueError`. Bound types are guaranteed int or None; prices and quantities are
integers (not bool); pair shapes are valid. Prices need not decrease.

- `breakdown(quantity) -> list[tuple[int, int, int]]`: return `(units, unit_cents,
  subtotal_cents)` for each used tier, in order, omitting tiers with zero units.
  A zero quantity gives `[]`; negative quantity raises `ValueError`.
- `quote(quantity) -> int`: sum the graduated subtotals. Example: tiers
  `[(10, 100), (20, 80), (None, 50)]` charge 1950 cents for 23 units.

Also implement:
- `format_money(cents) -> str`: integer cents formatted with exactly two decimals
  and a leading `$`, no grouping; negative cents raise `ValueError`.
- `format_invoice(table, items) -> str`: items is an iterable of `(label, quantity)`
  pairs. Labels are guaranteed strings without newlines. Each item is independently
  priced starting at the first tier; preserve order and repeated labels. Each line
  is exactly `LABEL: Q units = $D.CC` (always `units`, even for 1). End with
  `Total: $D.CC`. Join lines with `\n` and no trailing newline. Empty items produce
  `Total: $0.00`. Negative quantities raise `ValueError`.
